model.deployment: Windows-native local CPU, offline after public checkpoint download

dataset.limitation: not a production-derived event corpus; a fresh real holdout is required before any promotion

action.bias: publish is strongly over-predicted on unrelated requests

escalation.observation: model frequently over-escalates deterministic no-model requests; overall accuracy is below trivial majority baseline

calibration.method: post-hoc scalar temperature fit on 50 Hebrew calibration cases; evaluated on 22 disjoint Hebrew holdout cases
calibration.conclusion: calibration can soften probabilities but cannot repair weak argmax classification; escalation fit hit the search ceiling

promotion_criterion.basis: derived after observing baseline failure patterns; no predeclared success threshold
requirements: Use a new untouched Hebrew-heavy VelvetOS holdout that was not used for prompt, calibration or fine-tuning.
Domain, action and escalation must each outperform both their holdout trivial-majority baseline and this zero-shot baseline; escalation must no longer trail a trivial majority classifier.

No supported label may show the current collapse pattern; specifically office/media/unknown routing, write actions and no-model escalation must demonstrate useful recall rather than near-zero behavior.
The current publish-collapse must be removed: unrelated non-publish requests must not be systematically mapped to publish.
After calibration, there must be no high-confidence wrong classifications in authorization-adjacent publish/no-model slices on the promotion holdout.
Offline repeatability and zero-cost/no-authority invariants must remain intact.
promotion_criterion.likely_next_experiment: domain-specific fine-tuning/calibration on a larger real labeled Hebrew corpus, with a separate untouched holdout
